                        </ns0:gap> Zion. So Gr.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>every one of them</ns0:hi> in Zion appeareth before God <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This is here added as the blessed design and fruit of their long and tedious Journey, as that which put life into them, and made them bear all inconveniences with great chearfulness, they are all graciously admitted into the presence of God in <ns0:hi>Zion.</ns0:hi> But the words are and may be otherwise rendred, until every one of them <ns0:hi>appear before the God of gods in Zion.</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>the God of Gods shall be seen</ns0:hi> (or <ns0:hi>useth to appear,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>manifest himself:</ns0:hi> for the future Tense oft notes the continuance of the action) <ns0:hi>in Zion.</ns0:hi> Which is mentioned in the Close as the reason of that affection and industry which is described in the foregoing passages.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 O LORD God of hosts <ns0:hi>n</ns0:hi> hear my prayer: <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">In restoring me to thy House and service; which is my chief desire, <ns0:hi>Verse</ns0:hi> 2. 3.</ns0:note> give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>r</ns0:hi> Who canst easily remove and subdue those enemies of mine who banish and keep me from the place of thy wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 Behold, O God our shield, and look upon the face <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Do not turn away thine eyes from him as men do from those whom they hate or despise, but cast a favourable eye to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards him. By <ns0:hi>face</ns0:hi> he means either his person, the word <ns0:hi>face</ns0:hi> being oft redundant, as it is <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 43. 3. or his state and condition.</ns0:note> of thine anointed <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Either 1. Of Christ, whose proper name is <ns0:hi>the Messiah,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>the anointed.</ns0:hi> So the meaning may be, Lord, I deserve not one good look from thee, because by my great wickedness I have procured thy just displeasure, and this ba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishment; but look upon thy Christ, whose coming and me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ritorious passion, though future to us, is present to thee, and for his sake look upon me. Or, 2. Of me who, though a vile sinner, am thine anointed King. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 12. 7. <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 23. 1.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Understand <ns0:hi>elsewhere;</ns0:hi> which is necessary to compleat the sence: or, <ns0:hi>in the tents of wickedness;</ns0:hi> which may be supplied out of the next Clause. Such Ellipses are usual in Scripture, as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 91. 7. <ns0:hi>at thy side (i. e.)</ns0:hi> left side, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 19. 1, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>

                     </ns0:note> in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Than to live in the greatest glory and plenty and pleasure; which is ordinarily the lot of wicked men, as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> observed before, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 17. 14. <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 73 6, 7. and elsewhere.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 For the LORD God <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a sun <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">To enlighten and quicken and direct and comfort all his people; whereas they that live without God in the world <ns0:hi>Walk in darkness, and know not whither they go,</ns0:hi> as is said, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 12. 35.</ns0:note> and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 15. 1. Psal. 119. 114.</ns0:note> shield <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">To save his People from all their Enemies, and from those dreadful and deadly miseries which attend all o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther men.</ns0:note>: the LORD will give grace <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">His favour and friendship, which is better than life, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 63. 3. and all the blessed fruits of it.</ns0:note> and glory <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Not the Vain-glory and Splendour of this World, of which <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> would not have spoken so magnificently, because upon all oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casions he expresseth a great contempt of those things, but the honour which comes from God here, and that eternal and ineffable Glory lay'd up for God's People in the future world.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 34. 9, 10.</ns0:note> no good <ns0:hi>thing</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Nothing that is truly good in it self, and which is good for them: for sometimes afflictions, which are evil in themselves, are good and necessary, and highly advantageous to good men; and the good things of this world would do them much hurt: which is verified by frequent experiments.</ns0:note> will he withhold from them that walk uprightly <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">That worship God sincerely, and order their conversations aright. Which Clause <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> seems, to me, to add designedly to prevent or remove an objection against what he had now said, which might be taken from his own case, whereby it appeared that God was no such sun or shield to him, but exposed him to great and sore calamities. Which being certain and evident, <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid</ns0:hi> here assigns the true reason of it, which was not from any defect in God's goodness and sufficiency, but onely from his own gross miscarriages whereby he had clouded this sun, and cast away this shield, and forfeited these priviledges by depart<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing from his integrity.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 O LORD of hosts, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 2. 12.</ns0:note> blessed <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the man that trusteth in thee <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Who, though he be deprived of the opportunity of pay<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing that outward Worship to thee which is appropriated to thy House, yet giveth thee that inward worship which is more valuable in thy account, and placeth his chief trust and hope and happiness in thee alone.</ns0:note>
